segments.text: Hook: Every key press on the Enigma changed the electrical path through its rotors.
The Enigma was a cipher device used by Nazi Germany to protect military communication.
It scrambled the 26 letters of the Latin alphabet with a rotating rotor mechanism.
Each press shifted the rotors, so the same letter was encrypted differently each time.
The design made the machine highly resistant to conventional cryptographic attacks based on patterns.
Payoff: That design flaw – the fixed wiring – eventually gave codebreakers a clue.
